title: Armstrong as supreme improviser, I Can't Give You Anything But Love
summary: Both agree Armstrong was the greatest melodic improviser with form; Randolph points to his I Can't Give You Anything But Love as an eye-opener.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, Louis, of course, was probably the greatest improviser, melodic improviser, the world's ever known.
Wasn't he, though? And I'll tell you
And he had structure and form in his improvisations.
He certainly did. And you know what really brought that out, what opened my eyes on that? I guess you heard it too, is, 'I Can't Give You Anything But Love.'
He had the band saying (musical sounds), and while they're doing that, he says (musical sounds).
Yeah, just never-ending wonder. I mean, I've heard all the records, all my life. And I go back and listen to him again, and I still sit there and wonder.
